guardian_world.title: Extreme heat warnings issued for parts of southern California
guardian_world.description: Temperatures in US state forecast to hit high 30s celsius this week, while regions in Indonesia grapple with wildfiresThe National Weather Service in the US has issued extreme heat warnings for parts of southern California, including Los Angeles, until Thursday, as temperatures are expected to hit the high 30s celsius. Burbank, a suburb north of Los Angeles, recorded 39C on Saturday, a few degrees shy of the October record for the region set in 1987. A persistent area of high pressure will remain in place this week, leading to further hazardous hot weather and increased fire risk.Parts of Indonesia are in the midst of an extreme wildfire season, which has peaked over the past month. Western Kalimantan (Borneo) and southern Sumatra have been particularly badly affected. The lack of rainfall has dried the usually water-logged tropical soils, meaning that fires have been able to spread quickly, above and below the surface. Indonesia’s soils are also extremely rich in peat, meaning that the smoke produced from the fires contain higher levels of toxic gases such as sulphur dioxide and carbon monoxide. Cities in surrounding areas and as far as Malaysia and Singapore have experienced reduced air quality in recent weeks as a result. Drought and wildfires are more common in this part of the world during El Niño events owing to suppressed thunderstorm activity. Continue reading...

guardian_world.title: Trump approval ratings plummet to new low, polls show

The benchmark comes as neighboring New York declared a state of emergency about measles rates there.Pennsylvania’s health department said Monday 1,004 cases of measles had been confirmed. un_news.title: Security, sacrifice or opportunity: Visions differ over effective climate action
un_news.description: Should the world move away sharply from fossil fuels, or manage a slower, more careful retreat?

un_news.title: Extreme heat making pregnancy a ‘new fault line’ in climate crisis
un_news.description: Pregnancy and childbirth have become a “new fault line in the global climate crisis” as extreme heat worsens, the head of the UN climate action body (UNFCCC) warned on Monday, calling for maternal and newborn health to be built into countries’ climate plans.

un_news.title: ICC unseals four arrest warrants over Taliban persecution of women and girls
un_news.description: The International Criminal Court (ICC) has made public four arrest warrants against senior Taliban figures, accusing them of persecuting women and girls in Afghanistan, which amounts to a crime against humanity.

un_news.title: UN upholds housing as a human right on World Habitat Day
un_news.description: Representatives from governments, civil society and academia meeting in Muscat, Oman on Monday called for urgent action to address a global housing crisis affecting nearly 3.4 billion people.

un_news.title: Sudan: Driver killed in aerial attack on aid trucks in South Kordofan
un_news.description: The World Food Programme (WFP) has strongly condemned a deadly airstrike on two clearly marked aid trucks in South Kordofan, Sudan, this past weekend.

un_news.title: One day behind bars: Students and incarcerated women break prison stigma in Thailand
un_news.description: “Your mind follows the thread, one by one, row by row. You know? It’s like meditation. I don’t like machines.”

un_news.title: Beyond the Moon: Space Week around the world
un_news.description: Right after the Soviet Union launched Sputnik in 1957, UNOOSA, the UN Office for Outer Space Affairs, was established and has since been monitoring developments across more than 77 successful lunar missions and other journeys while also taking a lead role in the annual World Space Week, which runs from 4 to 10 October.

un_news.title: ‘He felt heard’: How a film brought a UN report to life in Xochimilco
un_news.description: A documentary drawn from United Nations University research was screened at the COP30 climate conference and film festivals across Europe. Its most important journey, though, was the one back to the Mexico City canals where it was filmed.

un_news.title: Rotting food waste emits 5 times more greenhouse gases than planes
un_news.description: Rotting food waste is causing up to 10 per cent of total global greenhouse gas emissions – five times more than the entire aviation sector, the UN’s environment agency warned this week.

un_news.title: Uganda’s UN-supported wildlife forensics lab turns ivory seizures into convictions
un_news.description: The package originated in Entebbe, Uganda, bound for Cairo, containing 10 kilograms of thumb-sized pieces that could have been either bone or elephant ivory.

un_news.title: ‘Money alone won’t get us there’: UN steps up aid for 12 forgotten crises
un_news.description: Getting aid to people in the world’s most neglected emergencies takes more than money. It takes open roads, open borders and leaders willing to help it reach those in dire need.

un_news.title: Global life expectancy bounces back to near pre-pandemic levels, WHO says
un_news.description: People around the world are living longer again, with global life expectancy almost fully recovered from the disruption of the COVID-19 pandemic, the World Health Organization (WHO) said on Friday.

un_news.title: Ukraine war ‘a human rights catastrophe’ that must end, says Türk
un_news.description: The war in Ukraine is a human rights catastrophe that is “growing and intensifying by the week” and threatening an even greater disaster across the region, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk said on Friday.

un_news.title: Collective action needed to tackle global information crisis, UN-led dialogue hears
un_news.description: Governments, UN entities, civil society, media, academia and the private sector have called for stronger cooperation and practical action to respond to a rapidly changing global information landscape.

un_news.title: World News in Brief: Cycle of violence continues in Haiti, seafarer deaths off Somalia, food insecurity in the Middle East
un_news.description: Haitians remain in the grip of lethal gang violence as it continues to “adapt and expand”, the UN’s top rights official, Volker Türk, said on Friday.

un_news.title: Escalating fighting in Yemen deepens food security crisis
un_news.description: Renewed conflict in Yemen has triggered a surge in hunger that could have consequences in the wider region and beyond, the World Food Programme (WFP) warned on Friday.

un_news.title: Gaza: WHO appeals for massive aid influx ahead of winter
un_news.description: Repeated delays in bringing lifesaving medicines, prosthetics and more from Israel into Gaza risk having devastating consequences on Palestinians who urgently need them in the war-torn enclave, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) said on Friday.

un_news.title: ‘I have not lost my dreams’: Refugee education funding cuts threaten millions
un_news.description: A teenage girl who fled war-torn Sudan for neighbouring Egypt and hopes to pursue a technology degree is an example of why countries must ensure that young refugees can continue to learn.

un_news.title: UN Member States weigh latest Security Council veto, this time on Iran
un_news.description: The General Assembly met on Thursday to examine the Security Council’s latest veto, cast by China and Russia over a United States-backed sanctions panel of experts on Iran nuclear facilities.

un_news.title: No more execution attempts on Christa Pike: UN rights chief

un_news.title: World News in Brief: Marshall Islands nuclear legacy, FlyDubai attack condemned, Ukraine update, breast cancer treatment expanded in West Bank

un_news.title: ‘Women are not victims’: Türk calls for women to be at the heart of peace and security
un_news.description: Women must be at the centre of efforts to prevent conflict and build lasting peace, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk said on Thursday.

un_news.title: Nepal floods threaten jobs and livelihoods beyond disaster zone: ILO
un_news.description: The deadly flash floods in northern Nepal have severely disrupted employment and livelihoods, with wider impacts beyond communities that were directly affected, the International Labour Organization (ILO) said in a preliminary assessment released on Thursday.

un_news.title: Ebola response faces setback as transit centre burns down in DR Congo camp

un_news.title: Who gets to shape AI? UN debate centres on power, trust and inclusion

un_news.title: World News in Brief: Storm clouds over Gaza, deadly obstacles face Mexican women rights defenders, Latvia booze ban proves lifesaver

un_news.title: Could a new global panel defuse inequality’s ‘ticking time bomb’?

un_news.title: Somali families face renewed violence amid worsening hunger crisis

un_news.title: Homicides fall as organised crime grows more profitable – and networked
